The same integer reduction applies to every consecutive contracting-to-contracting transition, yielding geometric differences and the strict necessary inequality \(H_{k-1}<(5-t)t^{k-1}\). For \(k\ge5\) the first four reciprocal powers contradict this inequality; for \(k=4\) the attracting multiplier gives \(t<3/4\), again a contradiction. The rational orbit with \(a=203/5000\) and \(b=17/25\) is exactly periodic, has strict +--- itinerary, four distinct points, and return multiplier \(344064/390625<1\). All boundary cases are excluded or explicitly handled. An exact standalone verifier confirms the example and fixed rational identities; universal quantification comes from proof, not sampling.
